title: Octave-scale audiogram roughness adds no demonstrated predictive value beyond bilateral hearing averages: temporal NHANES validation
abstract: Pure-tone averages discard audiogram shape. We tested the mean absolute second difference across five octave-spaced thresholds, averaged over both ears, as a predictor of concurrent self-reported hearing trouble. A survey-weighted logistic model trained in 3817 NHANES2011–2012 adults aged20–69 was transported unchanged to 4263 separately recruited NHANES2015–2016 adults. The baseline included age, sex, education, race/ethnicity, better- and worse-ear PTA4 and bilateral high-frequency thresholds. Adding roughness changed weighted Brier from 0.124570 to 0.124456 (delta-0.000114; approximate target-PSU95% interval-0.000317 to+0.000097; joint-refit interval-0.000383 to+0.000304). AUC changed by+0.000190. Superiority was not established. Flexible comparators and measurement restrictions test robustness but do not support a new clinical marker. This is a negative representation test of cross-sectional self-report, not proof of no auditory information; shared survey protocols limit external validity.
